task.description: HARD GATE. Run WF-02 Step 2d against this run's diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD, implementation commit 093b114) using .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions: idiomatic OTP/Ecto usage vs. crutch, supervision integrity, type-safety gaps, and scope creep -- plus consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ and docs/anti-patterns.md. Three specific rulings are wanted, each stated explicitly with reasoning: (1) whether the two indexes beyond the requirement's enumerated three are justified or scope creep; (2) whether the deliberate lowercase-status divergence from the shipped instance_projections convention is correct; (3) whether shipping a NOT NULL tenant_id that nothing can currently populate is acceptable to merge, or whether it should block this run.
acceptance_criteria: the diff is reviewed against reviewer.md's four questions, each answered explicitly
consistency with docs/migration/decisions/0003 (Decisions A, B, C) is checked and stated
docs/anti-patterns.md is checked against this diff
the three specific rulings above are each given with reasoning
non-blocking findings are recorded rather than silently dropped

WHERE id = $1 AND status = '<expected>'`), never a changeset-mediated read-modify-write, because that WHERE clause IS the concurrency control. That is precisely the shape reviewer.md question 1 exists to catch running the WRONG way: a `case status do` inside a changeset doing a state machine's job by hand would have been the crutch, and would have reintroduced the lost-update race. The diff avoids it and says why. Likewise InstanceDefinitionSnapshot exposes create_changeset/2 only -- no update_changeset/2, no generic changeset/2, no delete path -- so write-once is expressed as absent module surface rather than as a runtime flag or a DB trigger, matching 0003 Decision C clause 1's stated position. No @schema_prefix on either module (process_definition.ex:74-79, snapshot :80-85) is correct and non-obvious: the table lives in one Postgres schema per tenant, so a compile-time prefix would be the crutch and runtime `prefix:` is the idiom. Field/column type pairing (field(:tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) / add :tenant_id, :binary_id) matches the shipped instance_projection.ex convention. No idiom finding. === Q2 -- SUPERVISION INTEGRITY: PASS, confirmed rather than assumed. === Three independent checks, all run this session. (i) `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` filtered for application.ex / supervisor / process_instance returns NONE. (ii) `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/application.ex lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex lib/letflow/process_instance.ex` produces empty output while all three files exist -- i.e. present and untouched, not absent. (iii) grep over BOTH new modules for GenServer|gen_statem|spawn|Task.|Agent.|start_link|Supervisor|:ets|Process.|receive|send( returns zero hits. So: no process is added, no child spec is added to the supervision tree, no singleton or shared-state process appears, no unsupervised spawn exists, and per-instance isolation via Letflow.InstanceSupervisor is untouched by this diff. The only runtime execution these files gain is migration DDL, which runs under Ecto.Migrator -- already-supervised infrastructure this diff does not modify. Supervision integrity is intact. === Q3 -- TYPE-SAFETY GAPS: four recorded, none blocking. === (a) The load-bearing one. The Ecto.Enum dumped string and the SQL predicate literal in uq_active_definition are two INDEPENDENT literals in two different files (process_definition.ex:92-95 vs. 20260816193001:107-111). A stricter type system (Rust/OCaml) would not catch this either -- the predicate is an opaque string on both sides of the DB boundary -- so this is a gap no type system closes and only an exit-code test can. If they ever disagree the partial unique index matches zero rows and PD-03's single-active-per-name invariant is silently unenforced with no error anywhere. Step 1b already routed this to TEST-DESIGNER; I re-affirm it as a Step 3 requirement (assert pg_indexes.indexdef for uq_active_definition contains the literal WHERE status = 'active', plus a behavioural 23505 assertion on a second :active row with the same name). (b) Same shape: on_delete: :nothing -> :delete_all is a one-atom edit with no compile-time or test-time consequence today. Remedy: assert pg_constraint.confdeltype = 'a' for instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey. Also a Step 3 item. (c) `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}` on both modules (process_definition.ex:105, snapshot :106) is the field-less form, so Dialyzer cannot reject %ProcessDefinition{status: :retired} even though `@type status :: :draft | :active | :deprecated | :archived` is declared on the very next line (:106) and never attached to the field. This matches the shipped instance_projection.ex convention, so it is a project-wide pattern rather than a REQ-027 regression -- recorded per reviewer.md question 3's 'note it even if not asked', now that this is the third schema module to repeat it. (d) `graph` is an untyped string-keyed :map here while REQ-028's already-merged Letflow.Definitions.Graph is a real defstruct (nodes/edges), with no declared conversion between them. This is the textbook 'a stricter type system would have forced a serde boundary' case. Step 1b logged it as OQ-3 and deferred the conversion to REQ-029/REQ-030; the schema still DECIDES the column type rather than deferring it, so nothing is left unspecified in this diff. Watch item. === Q4 -- SCOPE CREEP: none. === The diff is exactly two migrations, two schema modules, and two appended manifest entries. Zero behaviour: no context module, no CRUD function, no query builder, no behaviour, no macro, no generic plumbing, no abstraction of any kind that a later requirement would have to unwind. reviewer.md question 4 targets abstractions and framework machinery arriving ahead of the stage that needs them; nothing here is an abstraction. The diff is also affirmatively anti-scope-creep: both moduledocs and both migration headers enumerate what deliberately does NOT exist and why -- no update_changeset/2 on the snapshot, no `belongs_to :definition` association (declined SPECIFICALLY to prevent Repo.preload/2 coupling across the snapshot->definition edge, which is the coupling PD-08 exists to break), no @schema_prefix, no CHECK constraint on graph, no FK on instance_id, no tenant_id on the snapshot table, and four-plus declined R-Co indexes. An implementer running away with scope does not write down the things it chose not to build. The shipped index set is SMALLER than R-Co's, not larger. Index question answered separately in Ruling 1. === RULING 1 -- THE TWO EXTRA INDEXES: JUSTIFIED, NOT SCOPE CREEP. === ELIXIR-DEV's load-bearing argument for idx_snap_definition VERIFIED and it holds. Postgres creates an index automatically only for PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints; a FOREIGN KEY constraint creates none on the referencing side (the referenced side must already have one, here process_definitions_pkey). Under NO ACTION -- which is what on_delete: :nothing emits, via connection.ex:1918's catch-all reference_on_delete(_), do: [] -- the RI check fired on a parent DELETE or PK UPDATE must locate referencing rows by instance_definition_snapshots.definition_id; with no index that is a full sequential scan per deleted parent row. Three things make this stronger than the abstract argument. (i) The path is real, not hypothetical: REQ-033 acceptance criterion 4 (docs/requirements.yaml, verified by direct read) is literally 'deleting the source process_definitions row ... does not remove or invalidate an existing snapshot row', which exercises the parent-delete path head-on. (ii) Cardinality points the wrong way without it: instance_definition_snapshots is one-row-per-INSTANCE and is by a wide margin the higher-cardinality table of the pair, so the unindexed seq scan is the expensive case, not the cheap one. (iii) In-repo precedent: the already-merged 20260816120004_create_event_payload_store.exs:82 creates a unique_index on its own FK column event_id -- indexing the referencing side of an FK is the established Letflow pattern, not an invention of this diff. idx_def_status verified against the cited source directly: R-Co migrations/004_definitions.sql:39 is `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_def_status ON process_definitions(status);`, present verbatim. idx_snap_definition likewise at 004:68-69. Both are ported, not invented. Both exist in lib/letflow/design/req027-definition-core-schema.md:365 and :494 and therefore passed the Step 1b design gate, which flagged them forward to this gate explicitly rather than letting me meet them first in the diff. RULING: not scope creep. An index is not an abstraction -- it adds no API surface, no module, no coupling, and nothing a later requirement must unwind; it is additive and independently revertible. REQ-027's description says 'Indexes: ...' and enumerates three but nowhere states that list is exhaustive, and acceptance criteria are satisfaction conditions, not ceilings. Both extras are R-Co-sourced, individually justified, and DISCLOSED -- in the migration headers (20260816193001:122-124, 20260816193002:109-112) and in the commit message -- rather than smuggled in. Decisive for me: the same diff DECLINES idx_def_name as redundant against the (name, version) btree's leading column, idx_def_fts on R-Co's own authority, and the four 028_adp02 tenant-prefixed variants as degenerate under Decision B, each with a citation. That is the behaviour of an implementer bounding scope, not exceeding it. CAVEAT recorded as a non-blocking note: idx_def_status is the weaker of the two. Its only consumer (REQ-030's list/1 ?status= filter) is unmerged, it is a four-value low-cardinality column a planner may well ignore in favour of a seq scan, and it partially overlaps uq_active_definition. It remains defensible (R-Co-sourced, disclosed, additive, and process_definitions is a low-write table so the per-row btree cost is negligible) but it is the one index here justified by a FUTURE requirement rather than by a property of the shipped schema. See issues. === RULING 2 -- THE LOWERCASE-STATUS DIVERGENCE: CORRECT, AND FORCED. === Mechanism re-derived from the vendored source, not from the design's claim. deps/ecto/lib/ecto/enum.ex init/1's first cond clause is `is_list(values) and Enum.all?(values, &is_atom/1) -> validate_unique!(values); {:string, Enum.map(values, fn atom -> {atom, to_string(atom)} end)}`. So values: [:draft, :active, :deprecated, :archived] (process_definition.ex:92-95) dumps :active as the lowercase "active". The migration's predicate is where: "status = 'active'" (20260816193001:109) and the column default is "draft" (:80). Self-consistent. The failure mode if they disagreed is exactly as stated: a partial unique index over zero rows, PD-03 silently unenforced. IS THE DIVERGENCE CORRECT? Yes, and it is FORCED rather than chosen. REQ-027 acceptance criterion 2 fixes the predicate literal as lowercase 'active' and the requirement description names the lowercase atoms; given that criterion, the bare atom-list Ecto.Enum form is the ONLY internally consistent option. The alternative (instance_projections' keyword-mapping form) would require changing an acceptance criterion, which an implementer may not do. IS SELF-CONSISTENCY THE RIGHT CONVENTION, RATHER THAN UNIFORM CASE? Yes -- and I go further than the diff's own framing: THE PREMISE THAT LOWERCASE IS THE DIVERGENCE IS ITSELF WRONG. I checked every status column shipped in this repo. 20260814000002_create_approvals.exs:9 default "pending"; 20260816000001_create_tenants.exs:30 default "active" with lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 bare atom list; 20260816000004_create_users.exs:40 default "active" with lib/letflow/identity/user.ex:38-39 bare atom lists; 20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs:43 default "ACTIVE" with instance_projection.ex:48 keyword-mapping form; 20260816193001:80 default "draft". Four of five shipped status columns are lowercase bare-atom. instance_projections is the OUTLIER, adopted deliberately for fidelity to R-Co's event-store payloads. REQ-027 therefore ALIGNS WITH THE MAJORITY convention. The migration header's framing ('Note this differs from 20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs') is factually accurate but reads as if REQ-027 were breaking a house style; it is not, and a future reader could be misled by it. Uniform case would in any event be the wrong convention to adopt: each table's stored case is constrained by what it must interoperate with (R-Co event payloads for projections; REQ-027's own acceptance criterion here), so forcing global uniformity would mean overriding an external constraint for cosmetic tidiness. Dump-predicate agreement WITHIN a table is the property that carries the invariant, and it is satisfied. IS THE CROSS-TABLE INCONSISTENCY A MAINTENANCE HAZARD WORTH RECORDING? Yes, but mild, and it is ALREADY recorded in three places a maintainer will actually be reading: the migration header (20260816193001:25-34), ProcessDefinition's dedicated moduledoc section (:30-50, which states 'Changing either one without the other is a defect'), and by cross-reference to the sibling. The residual hazard is not the case mismatch -- it is that the coupling is enforced by PROSE ONLY (Q3 item (a)). Non-blocking here: REQ-027's own acceptance criteria include no test, and Step 3 is the correct owner of the exit-code gate. === RULING 3 -- THE UNPOPULATABLE tenant_id: ACCEPTABLE TO MERGE. DOES NOT BLOCK REQ-027. === Reached independently, not by deferring to the fact that ISS-0025 (#83) exists or to SECURITY-REVIEWER's isolation-neutrality finding. The case FOR blocking, weighed genuinely: merging a table into which no INSERT can currently succeed is on its face shipping something knowingly broken, and acceptance criterion 1 ('applying cleanly') is satisfied trivially by an empty table without ever testing insertability. That is a real argument and I do not dismiss it. THE DECISIVE COUNTER, WHICH NEITHER ISS-0025 NOR STEP 2c WEIGHS: this property is NOT NEW TO REQ-027. I verified directly that priv/repo/migrations/20260816120001_create_events.exs:85 and 20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs:42 BOTH already ship `add :tenant_id, :binary_id, null: false` with no DB default, and their writer (REQ-025's append path) is likewise unimplemented. Those merged, at this same stage, on this same reasoning. Blocking REQ-027 for this would apply a standard to the third table that was not applied to the first two, and would retroactively imply REQ-023 should never have merged. A gate that changes its rule between two structurally identical diffs is not a gate. Three further reasons. (i) The column is REQUIRED by an active decision record: 0003 Decision B mandates retaining tenant_id inside each tenant schema, and R-Co's adp-02 lists process_definitions among the tables carrying one. Making it nullable or dropping it to make the table insertable today would silently contradict Decision B -- exactly what reviewer.md question 4 and the decision-record discipline exist to prevent. The 'fix' would be worse than the gap. (ii) The gap's true location is the REQUIREMENT SET, not this diff: REQ-030 owns create/1 and mentions tenant_id zero times (verified by direct grep over its requirements.yaml entry). No change to REQ-027's five acceptance criteria could close it, and an implementer cannot resolve it without making a schema/API decision that belongs to a design gate. (iii) Unblock-Everything's scope boundary (docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md:145-150) is squarely on point: this is a defect NOTICED, not one standing in the way -- all five of REQ-027's acceptance criteria are satisfiable and satisfied with the column exactly as shipped. The directive's own words: 'A defect you merely notice while working -- unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria -- is filed and forwarded, not fixed here ... It becomes its own later run, not an unbounded scope creep on this one.' Fixing it here would mean editing docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-030 parameters or building a session-GUC tenant-context mechanism affecting every tenant-scoped table -- the textbook unbounded scope creep the boundary forbids. ON 'IS THIS SHIPPING SOMETHING KNOWINGLY BROKEN?': I characterise it more precisely. It ships a table that no MERGED requirement writes to, which is the normal condition of a schema-only requirement mid-stage -- every S2 table is in that state until its writer lands. The NOT NULL makes the eventual writer's obligation explicit and unavoidable rather than deferred: it converts an open design question into a stop sign that fires on the first insert attempt. Combined with the failure being LOUD (a hard not_null_violation that no CI run or smoke test can miss, versus R-Co's session-GUC DEFAULT which stamps whatever tenant UUID the connection last held and thereby MISATTRIBUTES rather than rejects), the shipped state is a feature, not a defect. I reached the same conclusion as SECURITY-REVIEWER by a different route (requirement-set location + merged precedent, vs. its isolation-neutrality analysis), so the two corroborate rather than one deferring to the other. CONDITION I ATTACH, stronger than 'already filed': ISS-0025 must be resolved BEFORE REQ-030 OR REQ-025 IS CLAIMED -- not merely before REQ-030 ships -- and resolved ONCE, cross-cuttingly, because events, events_archive, instance_projections and process_definitions all share the property and choosing differently per table would be worse than any single option. ISS-0025 says this; I affirm it as a REVIEWER-side gating condition so it survives as more than a note inside an issue file. Not re-filed (ISS-0012..ISS-0027 are ORCH's). === DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY (0003 A / B / C): nothing silently contradicted. === DECISION A (Ecto-idiomatic redesign, names preserved): honoured. binary_id PK, Ecto.Enum for the status column -- literally A's named 'TEXT + comment-documented allowed values -> Ecto.Enum' swap -- Ecto.Migration DSL only with no execute/1, one schema-defining concern per migration (two tables, two files). R-Co names preserved verbatim: process_definitions, instance_definition_snapshots, definition_ver, snapshotted_at, and the index names uq_definition_version, uq_active_definition, idx_def_stage, idx_def_status, idx_snap_definition. OBSERVATION, not a contradiction: A describes `UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` -> binary_id as a drop-in with 'same generation semantics', but the diff drops the DB-level default entirely (20260816193001:39-42 discloses this) and generates in Ecto via @primary_key autogenerate: true, so a raw INSERT bypassing Ecto now gets no id. That is consistent with A's intent and identical to every other shipped Letflow table, so it is repo-wide practice rather than a REQ-027 divergence -- recorded for the record only. DECISION B (schema-per-tenant + retained intra-schema tenant_id): honoured on BOTH halves. Isolation half -- `if prefix() do` guard wrapping the whole change/0 body plus prefix: prefix() on the table and on every one of the five indexes, in both files. Retained-column half -- tenant_id NOT NULL on process_definitions. The snapshot table's OMISSION of tenant_id (20260816193002:67-73) is B applied PRECISELY rather than B ignored: B retains the column 'on the tables the adp-0x docs describe', and adp-02's table mapping lists six tables not including this one. The four 028_adp02 tenant-prefixed index variants are correctly declined with B's own reasoning (under B the Postgres schema IS the boundary, so a leading-tenant_id index degenerates to its non-tenant counterpart at strictly higher write cost). No contradiction. DECISION C (event-store tables get a distinct strategy): not engaged -- neither table is an event-store table; process_definitions is a regular CRUD table and instance_definition_snapshots is a write-once derived table. C's clause 3 is the relevant one (derived tables get the SAME DSL as regular tables, correctness invariant left to runtime) and is followed: no special migration treatment. Worth noting as positive consistency rather than mere absence of conflict: the diff applies C's clause-1 pattern -- immutability enforced at the module layer, not the migration layer -- to the snapshot table even though C scopes that clause to event tables. InstanceDefinitionSnapshot exposes no update path at all. That is the right generalisation of C, not a departure from it. === REQ-022 SECTION 4 BOTH-HALVES RULE, MANIFEST, @spec: all satisfied. === Guard half: both migrations wrap their ENTIRE change/0 body in `if prefix() do ... end` with no else branch (20260816193001:73-125, 20260816193002:88-117). Registration half: both appear in @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest as entries 8 and 9, in the three-element {version, module, filename} form that the module's own @doc explains is required (a bare {version, module} entry is loadable only by accident). ALL SEVEN PRIOR ENTRIES SURVIVE VERBATIM -- the manifest hunk is a pure append; the only '-' line touching it is the trailing-comma edit on entry 7. tenant_scoped_migrations/0's @spec is BYTE-IDENTICAL: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex | grep -E '^[+-].*@spec'` returns nothing, i.e. no @spec line was added or removed. The stale 'seven entries' prose was correctly updated to 'nine' in BOTH places it appears (the manifest header comment and the @doc), so documentation does not drift behind the data. Coverage confirmed rather than assumed: the shipped guard-policing test (test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs, describe 'section 4 guard pattern ...') iterates TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations(), runs each entry through Ecto.Migrator.run/4 with NO :prefix under a synthetic probe version, and asserts public_tables() == tables_before -- so it now polices REQ-027's two migrations with no test edit required. === docs/anti-patterns.md AGAINST THIS DIFF: all three entries clear, no new instance introduced. === (1) 'Reporting mix test as passing without running it' -- not an instance. Commit 093b114 quotes concrete numbers (271 passed against a 271 baseline, --warnings-as-errors 0, --check-formatted 0) and, more to the point, reports CATALOG evidence read back from a provisioned probe schema (the indexdef strings including `WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)`, and confdeltype='a' for the FK) rather than restating what the migration source says. That is verification against the artefact, which is what the entry demands. (2) 'Overwriting requirement_status.yaml instead of appending' -- not an instance; `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD -- docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` is `16  0`, sixteen insertions and ZERO deletions, a pure append. (3) 'Extrapolating handoff timestamps' -- not applicable to the implementation diff; my own completed_at is a fresh `date -u` reading taken immediately before writing this file. Worth recording positively: the diff's practice of writing down DECLINED options with citations (four-plus indexes, R-Co's 1106 cascade, the instance_id FK, a CHECK on graph, tenant_id on the snapshot table) is the direct antidote to the class of failure anti-patterns.md collects -- it makes a future agent's well-intentioned 'fix' discoverable as a regression BEFORE they make it. The 1106 cascade disclosure (20260816193002:29-36 and snapshot moduledoc :28-33) is the clearest example: an agent cross-checking Letflow against R-Co's LIVE schema would otherwise find a CASCADE there and 'correct' Letflow into data loss. === VERDICT === PASS. No genuine crutch (Q1), supervision intact and verified three ways (Q2), four type-safety gaps recorded and all Step-3-ownable (Q3), no scope creep (Q4). Ruling 1: the two extra indexes are justified, not scope creep -- the FK-referencing-side argument verified and strengthened. Ruling 2: the lowercase divergence is correct and forced; self-consistency is the right convention; and lowercase is in fact the repo's MAJORITY convention, with instance_projections the outlier. Ruling 3: the unpopulatable tenant_id is acceptable to merge and does not block REQ-027, on merged precedent, decision-record compulsion, requirement-set location, Unblock-Everything's scope boundary, and the loudness of the failure -- with a gating condition attached to ISS-0025. Decision records A/B/C consistent. Anti-patterns clear. Five non-blocking notes recorded in result.issues, none re-filing ISS-0012..ISS-0027. Next: route to TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3), which owns the two exit-code gates that would convert this diff's two prose-only invariants into mechanical ones.

issues.description: NEW (not ISS-0012..ISS-0027). The `graph` default literal %{"nodes" => [], "edges" => []} is written TWICE as two independent literals: priv/repo/migrations/20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs:82 (the DB-level column default) and lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex:98 (the Ecto struct default). Both are wanted -- they serve different layers, and R-Co carries the DB default too (004:19) -- but nothing ties them together. If a future change edits one, the other silently disagrees, and a row inserted outside Ecto would then have a different default graph shape than one inserted through it. This is the same CLASS of hazard as the status-case dump/predicate coupling (which the diff does document prominently) but it is not documented anywhere and is not covered by any existing issue. Recommended owner: TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3 -- assert the DB column default matches %Letflow.Definitions.ProcessDefinition{}.graph. Not a defect in the shipped code and not a Step 2d gate failure; both literals are currently identical and correct.

NEW (not ISS-0012..ISS-0027). Type-safety observation per reviewer.md question 3's 'note it even if not asked'. Both new modules declare `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}` (process_definition.ex:105, instance_definition_snapshot.ex:106) -- the field-less struct form -- so Dialyzer cannot reject %ProcessDefinition{status: :retired} even though `@type status :: :draft | :active | :deprecated | :archived` is declared on the very next line and never attached to the field. A stricter type system (Rust/OCaml) would catch at compile time what here only Ecto.Enum's runtime cast rejects, and only on the changeset path -- direct struct construction bypasses it entirely. This MATCHES the shipped lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex convention, so it is a project-wide pattern rather than a REQ-027 regression; recorded now because this is the third schema module to repeat it and the pattern is worth a deliberate decision rather than accretion. No action required in this run.

NEW (not ISS-0012..ISS-0027). Ruling 1 caveat, recorded so it is not lost in the PASS. Of the two indexes beyond REQ-027's enumerated three, idx_def_status (20260816193001:124) is materially weaker than idx_snap_definition: its only consumer is REQ-030's list/1 ?status= filter, which is unmerged; status is a four-value low-cardinality column a planner may well ignore in favour of a sequential scan; and it partially overlaps uq_active_definition. It remains justified (verbatim from R-Co migrations/004_definitions.sql:39, disclosed in the migration header and the commit message, additive, and process_definitions is a low-write table so the per-row btree cost is negligible), which is why this is a note and not a FAIL.
